original_question: What is the condition present in 30% of individuals with Klippel–Feil syndrome and over 40% of those with VACTERL association?

final_qi.question: What is the condition present in 30% of individuals with Klippel–Feil syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: About one-third of patients with Klippel–Feil syndrome exhibit Sprengel deformity—a congenital elevation of the scapula caused by incomplete caudal migration of the shoulder girdle during embryonic development. Epidemiological studies consistently report that roughly 30 % of individuals with Klippel–Feil have this associated musculoskeletal anomaly.

final_qi.question: What is the condition present in over 40% of individuals with VACTERL association?
final_qi.long_answer: Among the characteristic malformations that define VACTERL association, structural cardiac anomalies are especially common; epidemiologic studies show that more than 40 % of affected individuals have a congenital heart defect (e.g., ventricular septal defect, tetralogy of Fallot).
